ERock.why: Sells and operates modular natural-gas generator systems (RockBlock) as on-site bridge, prime and backup power for AI data centers; its backlog and sold-out capacity are driven by data-center power orders (e.g. Anthropic, Meta's El Paso campus).
ERock.evidence: CEO: 'We contracted with Anthropic for 470 MW of generation capacity for a new data center. We commenced construction on the 366 MW El Paso Electric project, supporting Meta's data center campus in El Paso.'

players.product: RockBlock modular natural-gas generator systems (designed, assembled, installed and operated turnkey with Granite software) for on-site bridge / prime and backup power at AI data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Inaugural earnings call. Q2 revenue $39.9 million, up 26% sequentially from $31.7 million, including customer deliveries completed ahead of schedule such as earlier-than-expected generator production for the El Paso Electric Meta project (CFO Ian Blakely: 'a timing shift rather than a higher level of production for the full year'). Power system sales revenue $26.5 million (+67% from Q1); ongoing services revenue $13.3 million (-15% sequentially, Q1 campaign work not recurring). Gross margin 18.6%, adjusted gross margin 22.2%; adjusted EBITDA -$14 million versus -$12.4 million in Q1.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $39.9 million (+26% QoQ); power system sales $26.5 million (+67%); services $13.3 million; gross margin 18.6%; adjusted EBITDA -$14 million

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted power system sales backlog a record approximately $1.7 billion at the end of Q2, up roughly 10x year-over-year and up $400 million quarter-over-quarter; backlog includes only firm orders. CFO: the majority of backlog converts to revenue by the end of 2027, with approximately $360 million-$390 million in 2026. Pipeline grew over 3x from 1Q to 2Q, with multiple large-scale hyperscalers, AI data labs and neoclouds, directly and via utility partners. Services renewal rate running at 100%; O&M contracts typically five to 15 years.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog ~$1.7 billion (~10x YoY, +$400 million QoQ); $360 million-$390 million converts in 2026; pipeline over 3x in 2Q

quarterly_data.signal: Initial full-year 2026 guidance: revenue $435 million-$465 million (midpoint approximately 2.5x year-over-year) and adjusted EBITDA $3 million-$9 million, reflecting a significant increase in generator deliveries and installations through year-end; adjusted EBITDA expected to turn positive in the second half of 2026 as multiple large data center projects are executed. CFO: 'we continue to see positive trends in pricing and gross margin' on deals being negotiated, with the impact 'more 2028 and beyond' because the company is sold out through 2027 and into early 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $435 million-$465 million; adjusted EBITDA $3 million-$9 million; EBITDA positive in 2H 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: 'With the addition of the Anthropic contract, our production capacity is sold out through 2027 and into 2028.' CEO John Carrington: assembly expansion is triggered when capacity is '65% contracted or more'; a new facility can be ramped 'in a 12-month timeline at 1.2 GW at a cost of $15 million-$20 million', potentially sited closer to customers. Year-to-date capex $9 million, around $7 million of it for the Hyperion facility, with less than $10 million more to fully build it out.
quarterly_data.figure: production capacity sold out through 2027 and into 2028; new 1.2 GW facility in 12 months for $15 million-$20 million

quarterly_data.signal: Generator assembly moved in Q2 into the new Hyperion facility in Northwest Houston, which is targeted to increase annual assembly capacity to approximately 1.2 GW by the end of this year at a cost of only $15 million in additional capital.
quarterly_data.figure: Hyperion assembly capacity ~1.2 GW by end of 2026; $15 million additional capital

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the market: AI-driven demand has pushed load growth to the highest levels in over 50 years; 'Supply chain constraints have extended gas turbine lead times to over four years' and interconnection queues 'can extend to over seven years', accelerating speed-to-power needs for hyperscalers, utilities and C&I customers. On deal size: training projects 'anywhere from five to over a gig', inference somewhat smaller, with momentum toward multi-phase and larger projects; training is 'still the lion's share' of demand. President Corey Amthor: increased utility interest over the last six months, often for in-front-of-the-meter peaker-style grid support; hyperscalers ask utilities for recommendations and 'ERock continues to be the one they're recommending' (CEO). Texas Batch Zero comments have had 'no impacts' so far.
quarterly_data.figure: gas turbine lead times over four years; interconnection queues over seven years (CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: Company profile and technology (management): 15-year operating history, over 400 operational sites and more than 1 GW of installed capacity with five nines of reliability. The proprietary RockBlock natural-gas generator can take full electrical load in as little as 10 seconds versus up to 45 seconds for competing gas solutions, and is engineered for transient response to match AI training and inference load swings, needing 'fewer or no batteries'. Management calls it 'the first natural gas engine on the market' to meet the California CARB DG standard, up to 99% cleaner than diesel, no water use, building blocks as small as 500 kW and approximately 50% smaller footprint. One asset serves bridge (prime) power until grid interconnection, then backup and dispatchable capacity. Nearly 150 MW deployment with the California Department of Water Resources, with approximately 50 MW installed in two days at the first site.
quarterly_data.figure: 400+ sites, more than 1 GW installed; full load in as little as 10 seconds; ~150 MW California DWR deployment

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Meta (via utility El Paso Electric, the purchaser): CEO: construction commenced on 'the 366 MW El Paso Electric project, supporting Meta's data center campus in El Paso'. El Paso Electric faced an estimated five-year timeline to deliver grid interconnection for the 366 MW Meta data center complex; 'EPE purchased our systems', and ERock is on track to commission the site in approximately 15 months, 'about four years faster than waiting on the grid'. During the bridge period El Paso Electric collects payments from Meta via PPA; after grid interconnection the asset can move into the utility's rate base as peak capacity.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: end customer (systems purchased by El Paso Electric)

connects_to.relationship: on-site natural-gas generation equipment (RockBlock generators) for a new Anthropic data center

contracts.signal: CEO: 'We contracted with Anthropic for 470 MW of generation capacity for a new data center'; 'we received an order for approximately 470 MW from Anthropic... This order reflects the equipment purchase agreement only'; installation and service agreements 'are typically negotiated and signed separately, and we expect those to follow in the normal course.' Anthropic is a new customer ('a generator-only agreement at this point') and is not the unnamed multi-phase 'customer A' referenced in the IPO. 'Anthropic selected ERock to ensure power supply certainty for their quickly growing compute needs.' CFO: with the Anthropic contract, production capacity is sold out through 2027 and into 2028.
